transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Hi. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I guess what really pushed me to come in today is that... well, I work as a receptionist, and lately, every time a heavy door slams or someone rolls a suitcase really fast across the lobby, I just jump. 

It feels like it’s happening all over again. My heart just starts pounding, and it takes me a good minute to get my heart rate back down and actually focus on my work again. It's just been really hard to deal with.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about these physical reactions happening again, even when you're not at work?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I sit around worrying about my heart pounding when I'm at home. It's more just... it catches me off guard when it actually happens at the desk. But once I'm off the clock and in a quiet place, I'm not really stressing about whether it's going to happen again. It just kind of hits me in the moment when I hear those loud noises.
When you're at work and you're in the environment where these loud noises happen, do you find yourself feeling anxious or on edge, worrying that another one of these reactions might happen again?

Not really, no. I mean, I'm just doing my job—answering the phones, pointing people in the right direction. I'm not sitting there waiting for my heart to start pounding or worrying about if I'm gonna jump. 

It's just... when the loud noise actually happens, that's when it gets me. But before that, I'm just working. I don't feel like I'm constantly on edge about having another reaction, it just catches me completely by surprise when it does happen.
Outside of work, in quieter or more relaxed settings, do you still find yourself easily startled or unusually alert to sounds or movements around you?

No, not really. Um, when I'm at home or just hanging out, it's usually pretty quiet, so I don't really notice myself jumping at things. I don't feel like I'm on high alert or anything like that when I'm just relaxing. It really just seems to be those specific loud bangs at the office.
When you're not at work and in calm environments, do you ever experience sudden episodes of intense fear, shortness of breath, or a racing heart without an obvious cause?

No, I haven't had anything like that. Um, if I'm at home or somewhere calm, my breathing and heart rate are totally normal. I don't get those sudden feelings of fear out of nowhere. It's really just... well, like I said, it's just tied to those loud noises at the front desk. Outside of that, I feel completely fine.
